about: The coverage each assembly must stay at or above. Checked by .github/scripts/coverage-floor.js, which the coverage workflow runs. One entry per assembly, never one number for the repository: the host project's pages and controllers are covered through API tests, and a combined figure would let engine coverage fall while the total held steady.
howToRaise: A floor is measured, never chosen. Run the coverage command below, read the score off the report, round it DOWN to two decimals and write that. Raise a floor in the same change that raises the coverage; a floor above the measured score reds the check immediately, which is the mistake this sentence exists to prevent.
command: dotnet test --configuration Release --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage" --results-directory TestResults && node .github/scripts/coverage-floor.js TestResults

Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.measured: line-rate 0.7111 and branch-rate 0.875 on the <package> tag of coverage.cobertura.xml, from the command above, run on Windows against net10.0.
Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.lineNote: Both figures moved DOWN when #68 split the solution, and neither is the suite weakening: the validator, the document, the validation result and the error type are the same code with the same tests, measured under Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.Engine below rather than here. What is left in this assembly is Plugin.cs at line-rate 0.0714, which needs a server to construct, RuleDocumentStore at line-rate 1, and the configuration class. The host share of the old combined figure was always this number; the combination was hiding it, which is the reason the file next to this one gives for never recording one score for the repository.
Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.branchNote: Every branch point left in this assembly is in RuleDocumentStore, at branch-rate 0.875. Plugin.cs reports branch-rate 1 over the branches it declares. The report puts what is unexecuted on one line, RuleDocumentStore.cs:128 at condition-coverage 83.33% (10/12), which is the six-clause name check that refuses a name composing into a path outside the store's directory. It short-circuits on the first clause that matches, so a name refused by an early clause never reaches the later ones and no set of inputs lights every slot.

Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.Engine.measured: line-rate 0.9948 and branch-rate 0.9791 on the <package> tag of coverage.cobertura.xml, from the command above with --framework net10.0 added, run on Windows. Only that target framework was measured: the machine this was run on has no .NET 9 runtime, so the net9.0 leg of the same command reports that the framework is missing rather than a score. An earlier version of this entry claimed both legs agreed and this one does not claim it.
Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.Engine.branchNote: The only partially covered branch point in the assembly is still the discard in the value-kind description in RuleDocumentValidator, reported as RuleDocumentValidator.cs:198 at condition-coverage 87.5% (7/8). The compiler requires it for exhaustiveness and no input reaches it, because a member that is absent is refused before anything describes its kind. Its line number moves whenever anything is added above it in that file and the arm itself has not changed since it was written.
Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.Engine.lineNote: The floor is raised in the same change that raises the coverage rather than left where it was, which is what the note above this one asks for. The one line at hits=0 in the whole assembly is RuleDocumentValidator.cs:206, the arm the branch note describes. Everything else is executed, including CollectionRefreshGate, MembershipApplier, ICollectionMembershipWriter, CollectionRefresh, CollectionRefreshOutcome, MembershipDiff, RuleDocument, RuleDocumentValidation and RuleValidationError. One thing worth knowing about the number rather than the code: when #38 put the gate in front of the applier, a run cancelled before it starts stopped entering the applier at all, which left the applier's own rethrow arm unexecuted and the line figure BELOW the floor of the day. What repaired it was not the gate's own lines but the test added with them, which cancels a run while it is writing.
